# MCP tool reference

The 14 tools the server offers, read from a running server.

The server is the same code as the CLI, over stdio. Start it with `agent-slack mcp`, or install it into a client
with `agent-slack mcp install --client claude-code`.

**Every call takes `workspace`.** There is no default workspace. **No tool posts**: `slack_post_prepare` returns
a preview, and posting, reacting, approving and connecting a workspace are CLI commands a person runs.

## Tools

| Tool | What it does |
|---|---|
| [`slack_workspaces_list`](#slack_workspaces_list) | The connected Slack workspaces, what each may do (`read` cannot post at all — Slack enforces that), and whether its credential looks healthy. |
| [`slack_channels`](#slack_channels) | Channels and conversations this account can see. |
| [`slack_read`](#slack_read) | Recent messages, newest first. |
| [`slack_thread`](#slack_thread) | One thread, parent first. |
| [`slack_search`](#slack_search) | Slack’s own search, in Slack’s syntax. |
| [`slack_people`](#slack_people) | Members of the workspace. |
| [`slack_files`](#slack_files) | Files this account can see. |
| [`slack_post_prepare`](#slack_post_prepare) | Compose a message, store it as a local draft, and return the preview a person must approve. |
| [`slack_draft_list`](#slack_draft_list) | The drafts held on this machine for this workspace, newest first. |
| [`slack_draft_get`](#slack_draft_get) | One draft, exactly as it would be posted, and the text it was written from. |
| [`slack_draft_delete`](#slack_draft_delete) | Throw a draft away. |
| [`slack_mode`](#slack_mode) | Reports whether this workspace can post, upload or react, and what its recorded grant allows. |
| [`slack_mode_request_send`](#slack_mode_request_send) | Returns the steps a **person** must take to let this workspace post. |
| [`slack_mode_narrow`](#slack_mode_narrow) | The path back to read-only. |

### `slack_workspaces_list`

The connected Slack workspaces, what each may do (`read` cannot post at all — Slack enforces that), and whether its credential looks healthy.

*read-only*

Takes no arguments.

### `slack_channels`

Channels and conversations this account can see. Bounded; `complete: false` means more remain.

*read-only*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `workspace` | string | no | which workspace, as `organisation/slack` |
| `all` | boolean | no |  |
| `limit` | integer | no |  |

### `slack_read`

Recent messages, newest first. Each arrives inside an untrusted-content envelope. `mismatch` means the message says different things in the channel and in its notification; `unrenderable` means part of it could not be shown.

*read-only*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `workspace` | string | no | which workspace, as `organisation/slack` |
| `channel` | string | **yes** | the channel id |
| `limit` | integer | no |  |
| `oldest` | string | no |  |
| `latest` | string | no |  |
| `cursor` | string | no |  |

### `slack_thread`

One thread, parent first. On a continuation page there is no parent, and every row is a reply.

*read-only*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `workspace` | string | no | which workspace, as `organisation/slack` |
| `channel` | string | **yes** |  |
| `ts` | string | **yes** | the parent message timestamp |
| `limit` | integer | no |  |
| `cursor` | string | no |  |

### `slack_search`

Slack’s own search, in Slack’s syntax. The query is sent verbatim.

*read-only*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `workspace` | string | no | which workspace, as `organisation/slack` |
| `query` | string | **yes** |  |
| `limit` | integer | no |  |
| `page` | integer | no |  |

### `slack_people`

Members of the workspace. Display names and statuses are editable by anyone and are treated as untrusted.

*read-only*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `workspace` | string | no | which workspace, as `organisation/slack` |
| `limit` | integer | no |  |

### `slack_files`

Files this account can see. URLs are carried, never fetched.

*read-only*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `workspace` | string | no | which workspace, as `organisation/slack` |
| `channel` | string | no |  |
| `limit` | integer | no |  |
| `page` | integer | no |  |

### `slack_post_prepare`

Compose a message, store it as a local draft, and return the preview a person must approve. **Nothing is posted.** The preview says how many people it would interrupt; show it in full and wait.

*writes*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `workspace` | string | no | which workspace, as `organisation/slack` |
| `channel` | string | **yes** |  |
| `text` | string | **yes** |  |
| `threadTs` | string | no |  |
| `mentionUsers` | string[] | no | user ids to mention, by id — never by name |
| `broadcast` | `here` \\| `channel` \\| `everyone` | no | interrupts the room; needs a person |

### `slack_draft_list`

The drafts held on this machine for this workspace, newest first. Nothing in them has reached Slack.

*read-only*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `workspace` | string | no | which workspace, as `organisation/slack` |

### `slack_draft_get`

One draft, exactly as it would be posted, and the text it was written from.

*read-only*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `workspace` | string | no | which workspace, as `organisation/slack` |
| `draftId` | string | **yes** |  |

### `slack_draft_delete`

Throw a draft away. One too damaged to read is removed too, unless it names another workspace, and the result says so. An approval prepared from it can no longer be used, because there is nothing left to post.

*writes · destructive*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `workspace` | string | no | which workspace, as `organisation/slack` |
| `draftId` | string | **yes** |  |

### `slack_mode`

Reports whether this workspace can post, upload or react, and what its recorded grant allows.

*read-only*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `workspace` | string | no | which workspace, as `organisation/slack` |

### `slack_mode_request_send`

Returns the steps a **person** must take to let this workspace post. Performs nothing: widening is a new OAuth grant approved in Slack’s own UI, and an agent never widens. Show these steps and stop.

*read-only*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `workspace` | string | no | which workspace, as `organisation/slack` |
| `port` | integer | no |  |

### `slack_mode_narrow`

The path back to read-only. Tightening needs nobody’s consent, but Slack never removes a scope from a token — only removing the app’s installation resets it — so this returns the steps rather than pretending to do it.

*read-only*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `workspace` | string | no | which workspace, as `organisation/slack` |
| `port` | integer | no |  |
